# Dozo

> Dozo is a workspace of always-on AI bots. Each bot keeps its conversation, memory and routines, does real work on a computer of its own (a sandboxed machine with a browser, files and a terminal), and asks the person before anything consequential. It is for people and small teams who want AI helpers that stay around and finish tasks instead of answering one prompt at a time.

Dozo is source available: its own files are under the Elastic License 2.0, the code it builds on under Apache-2.0. It is not open source. The licence does not allow offering Dozo to others as a hosted service.

## How it works

- Each bot has its own computer. You can watch its screen, take control and hand it back.
- A bot asks before it acts on anything that matters. You approve, edit or deny.
- Routines run a bot on a schedule. Bots keep memory between chats.
- Bots use your own model connection (your key or your subscription); model costs come from there.
- The desktop app can run the server on your own computer, so chats and files are stored there; what is sent to a model goes to the provider you chose (a local model stays on the computer).

## Apps

- Web app: https://app.dozo.bot (sign-up is open)
- Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux: https://github.com/SSilistre-dev/dozo/releases/latest . It opens the hosted server, your own server, or runs a server on your computer. The macOS build is signed; the Windows and Linux builds are not signed yet.
